title: Console UX: route-level quantization enablement (toggle, canary, permissions, audit log, warnings)
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
## Summary
We need a clear, safe Console UX for enabling quantization per route (opt-in, route-scoped). This ticket defines product requirements for permissions, audit visibility, default states, warnings/guardrails, and the minimum interactions needed for beta.

This UX is a primary safety mechanism for customers adopting the Quantization Profile Library: they must be able to enable quantization only on specific non-interactive workloads (e.g., batch summarization), canary it, and roll back quickly if quality regressions appear.

## Goals
- Make it easy to enable/disable quantization per route with clear state visibility.
- Encourage safe rollout (canary %) and rapid rollback.
- Ensure all changes are auditable (who/when/what changed) and permissioned (RBAC).
- Provide contextual warnings about quality/output-format risks (JSON/tool calling, long-context) without blocking legitimate use.

## Non-goals (v1 beta)
- No in-Console authoring or upload of user-supplied quantization profiles (library is Redwood-published only).
- No per-request override UI (headers/params) beyond what API standards decide; Console should configure route policy, not debug headers.
- No complex multi-arm experiments UI beyond a single canary percentage gate.

## User / Persona
- ML/platform engineer at customer enabling cost optimization for specific background routes.
- SRE/infra engineer needing confidence that changes are reversible and tracked.

## Primary UX surface area
Route Settings → "Optimization" (or "Model execution") section:
- Quantization: [Off | On] (toggle)
- Canary rollout: slider or numeric input (0–100%) shown only when quantization is On
- Status + details: shows whether traffic is running baseline vs quantized path, and which profile is currently active

## Required UX requirements
### 1) Default states
- Default for all existing routes: Quantization = Off.
- New routes created after feature launch: Quantization = Off.
- If org-level default is introduced later, Console must still show the effective resolved value at the route.

### 2) Toggle behavior (route-scoped)
- Toggle labeled: "Enable quantization" with a short helptext:
  - "Uses Redwood-published quantization profiles when compatible. Requests fall back to baseline automatically if incompatible."
- When turned On:
  - Show canary control (default 0% or 10% — decision below).
  - Show warning panel (see section 5).
  - Show "Active profile" field in a read-only manner (auto-selected) for beta.
- When turned Off:
  - Canary controls hidden/disabled.
  - Execution returns to baseline.

Open decision (needs alignment with Rollouts PM Paula Mendes + SRE):
- Canary default when enabling quantization:
  - Option A: default 0% and require user to explicitly set >0%
  - Option B: default 10% with explicit confirmation modal

### 3) Canary control requirements
- Inputs:
  - Slider 0–100% with numeric entry support.
  - Presets recommended: 0%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 100%.
- Copy:
  - "Canary % of requests" with helptext: "Only this percentage will attempt quantized execution. Others run baseline."
- Validation:
  - 0–100 inclusive only.
  - If quantization is On and canary is 0%, Console should display a non-blocking info note: "Quantization enabled but not receiving traffic."
- Safety affordance:
  - A prominent "Disable quantization" action near the canary control (one-click rollback), with confirmation.

### 4) Permissions / RBAC
- Only users with route-config write permissions can change settings.
- Users without write permissions:
  - Must still see effective state (On/Off + canary % + last changed by/time).
  - Controls disabled with tooltip: "You don’t have permission to edit route settings."
- If a user can edit routes but not org-level settings:
  - They can still edit route-level quantization when allowed by policy.

### 5) Warnings / guardrails (customer-facing)
When enabling quantization (or when setting canary >0%), show a warning panel with:
- General warning:
  - "Quantization can change output quality and formatting. Start with a canary and monitor error rates and quality metrics."
- Specific risk callouts (non-blocking):
  - "Structured output (JSON mode/tool calling) may be more sensitive to quantization."
  - "Long-context routes may see different performance characteristics."
- Linkouts:
  - "View quantization monitoring dashboard" (deep link to route-level metrics page)
  - "Rollback guidance" (link to docs or runbook excerpt)

### 6) Audit log visibility
- Every change must create an audit event with:
  - Route identifier, old value, new value
  - Actor (user/service), timestamp
  - Source: Console vs API
- Console UI requirements:
  - From the route settings page, include "View audit log" link filtered to that route.
  - Audit list must be filterable by: date range, actor, and setting type (quantization toggle vs canary %).

### 7) Effective state + runtime status visibility
Console should distinguish between:
- Configured state (what user set)
- Effective execution status (what is actually happening)

Minimum beta display:
- "Configured": On/Off + canary %
- "Execution":
  - "Quantized (profile: <id/version>)" when quantized path is active
  - "Baseline" when disabled or when the system is falling back
  - "Partially quantized" when canary <100%

If execution is falling back due to incompatibility:
- Show a warning badge: "Falling back to baseline" with a tooltip describing common causes (hardware incompatibility, profile unavailable).

### 8) Error states / validation messaging
When save fails, Console must show:
- Field-level inline errors when possible (e.g., canary out of range)
- Global error for server-side issues with request ID for support

Common errors to map to friendly messages:
- "Quantization not available for this model" → "Quantization is not yet supported for the model used by this route."
- "Insufficient permissions" → "You don’t have permission to change this setting."
- "Conflicting org/customer override" → "This setting is controlled by an organization policy."

## Analytics / instrumentation requirements (Console)
- Track events:
  - Viewed quantization settings
  - Toggled quantization on/off
  - Changed canary percentage
  - Clicked audit log link
  - Clicked monitoring dashboard link
- Include route id + org id (and whether change succeeded).

## Acceptance criteria
- Route settings page shows quantization section with:
  - Toggle, canary control, warnings, and read-only active profile/status.
- RBAC: users without write access cannot change settings but can view effective state.
- Audit log entries are created for changes and discoverable from the route.
- Clear warnings appear when enabling quantization / increasing canary >0%.
- Error states are actionable and map backend errors to understandable text.

## Open questions
1) Canary default (0% vs 10% with confirmation). Need decision from SRE (Sean Gallagher) + Rollouts PM (Paula Mendes).
2) Do we expose "profile selection" in Console for beta (Auto only vs allow choosing int8 vs int4 when multiple are available)? Current proposal: Auto only.
3) Where does quantization live in Console IA: "Optimization" vs "Model" vs "Advanced"? Design to propose.

comments: 2025-01-24 - Kenji Nakamura: Drafting initial IA proposal. Leaning toward placing under Route Settings → Optimization with "Cost/Latency" grouping; will share mocks in DES-211.
2025-01-27 - Paula Mendes: Canary default needs to be conservative. Preference: default 0% and require explicit canary >0 with confirmation copy. Avoid surprise behavior when toggling On.

2025-01-28 - Dylan Brooks: +1 on distinguishing Configured vs Effective. We’ve had confusion with fallback states in other features. We can reuse the existing "Effective config" component used for rollout policies.
2025-02-03 - Sean Gallagher: Audit log link from the route page is required for on-call. Also want the rollback action to be prominent and not hidden under overflow menus.

2025-02-06 - Nikhil Sharma: Confirmed beta requirement: Auto profile selection only; no manual int4/int8 picker. If multiple profiles exist, runtime chooses best compatible; Console surfaces the active one read-only.

2025-02-11 - Kenji Nakamura: Mocks in progress in DES-211. Added warning copy variants for JSON/tool calling sensitivity and a "View monitoring" linkout. Requesting feedback on canary control layout (slider vs presets).
